analysis.title: FX Daily: Dollar showing resilience to tech stock instability
key_insights: A poor start to the week for tech stocks caused some dovish repricing in the front end of the USD curve, but the dollar kept its momentum. The sell-off spread to broader US and global equities, so the dollar benefited from its safe-haven role.

ING still sees the AI story as the factor with the best potential to hit the dollar. Further weakness in tech/AI stocks should make more dollar appreciation less sustainable because it drives more dovish Fed repricing.

Nvidia's quarterly earnings are today's main focus. The company's long-term prospects are under more scrutiny after CEO Jensen Huang's departure. Speculation that he might be reinstated was dismissed yesterday.
ING expects some dollar stabilisation rather than another major leg higher. Because the dollar's bullish momentum is macro-driven, corrections may be easier to fade.

EUR/USD briefly dipped below 1.100 yesterday without enough bearish fuel for a sustained break. The short-term EUR:USD rate differential tightened by about 5bp in favour of the euro, so ING is not calling another leg lower yet.

Markets price 70bp of ECB tightening over the next 12 months, with a follow-up hike after December expected only in March. ING sees the EUR front end as more vulnerable to dovish repricing if oil prices fall again.

UK jobs data were weaker than expected but are unlikely to change Bank of England tightening plans. October payrolls fell 34k, September was revised up from 10k to 20k, September unemployment was 4.6%, and weekly earnings ex-bonus slowed from 3.7% to 3.5%.

BoE pricing remains aggressive, with an 80% implied probability of a December hike and 90bp of tightening over 12 months. ING's baseline is the next move in February, with risks of an earlier hike. Tomorrow's October UK CPI is expected to rise from 3.5% to 3.6%.

NOK is the worst-performing G10 currency since the start of November, down 4.7% vs USD and 3.3% vs EUR. The main driver is the sharp drop in oil prices, along with hawkish Fed repricing and unstable risk sentiment. ING sees downside risks persisting as Norges Bank has signalled more caution on further tightening.
ING's EUR/NOK year-end target is 10.65, with risks skewed toward 10.70-10.75 in the coming weeks. ING sees NOK facing more downside vs USD.
